messages:
Maria Chen: Quick UX nit - the y-axis compacting to K/M is fine, but the hover 'precision hint' is misleading. It shows `~1.2K` on hover but the tooltip text says `1,234` sometimes and `1.2k` other times. Feels inconsistent.
Tyler Nguyen: +1 saw this on the dashboard. Hover copy flips between full integer and compact depending on zoom level.
Arun Patel: Is this coming from the number formatter or the renderer? I think we format for axis labels and then reuse that for hover; should be separate.
Olivia Ramos: For accessibility we should expose the full numeric value to screen readers even if visually we show compact units. So hover should always have full literal number and an optional compact label.
Maria Chen: Proposal: visual label = compact (1.2K), hover title = exact value (1,234) and a small microcopy line with unit context e.g., "requests/min".
Tyler Nguyen: What about decimals? For values like 1234 we show 1.23K with two decimals on the axis sometimes. That makes the hover confusing when it shows 1,234. Should hover match decimals? I'm leaning to full integer to avoid rounding ambiguity.
Arun Patel: I think hover should be unambiguous and consistent. Suggestion: primary hover line = full integer (with separators), secondary line = compact variant + source (e.g., '≈1.23K · avg per min').
Olivia Ramos: Also a11y: screen reader text should read "one thousand two hundred thirty four requests per minute" not "one point two k". We'll need an aria-label override.
Maria Chen: UX copy options (short):
  - Option A: "1,234 requests/min"
  - Option B: "1,234 (≈1.23K) — requests/min"
  - Option C: "≈1.23K (actual 1,234)"
Which do we prefer?
Tyler Nguyen: I like B - explicit and shows both. But visual noise could be bad when there are many tooltips on small sparklines.
Arun Patel: For compact sparklines maybe show just compact on hover, but include a small chevron or "more" that reveals full value. On larger charts show both by default.
Olivia Ramos: That adds interaction complexity. For keyboard users, "more" needs to be focusable. Might be okay as long as it's consistent across chart types.
Maria Chen: Another related thing: when an outlier causes y-axis to autoscale, we often show axis ticks like 0, 50K, 100K where most points are <1K. People suggested adding a "clamp" badge in the legend - do we want that?
Tyler Nguyen: I prefer a per-chart control: a small toggle in the top-right: "Clamp outliers". Default off. If enabled, we show a small icon next to the axis e.g., ⚠️ (or ‹clamped›) - and tooltip explains: "Values above N have been clipped to improve trend visibility. Hover for actual values.".
Arun Patel: Implementation note: when clipping we should still keep the y-scale consistent for programmatic comparisons. Also need to emit metric/annotation so customers know clipping occurred.
Olivia Ramos: Copy for clamp tooltip draft: "Chart trimmed extreme values to surface typical trends. Full values available on hover or in raw table." Short and friendly.
Maria Chen: A visual accessibility nit: gridlines are currently #E6E6E6 and nearly invisible on some monitors. For contrast we should move to #D0D7DE or increase weight 1px -> 1.5px for major gridlines.
Tyler Nguyen: +1, but check with dark mode palette - we need tokens for light/dark.
Arun Patel: I'll add a design token PR for gridline-color and gridline-weight with responsive tokens for theme.
design-bot: Deploy preview available at https://preview.redwood-inference.design/charts/hover-precision-2024 - includes Option B tooltip and clamp toggle mockups. Use branch charts/hover-precision.
Olivia Ramos: Reviewed preview - spacing looks cramped on narrow panels. If we show both full and compact values the tooltip width jumps a lot. Consider making compact copy a muted second line to reduce width.
Maria Chen: Final asks for engineering: (1) hover always exposes full number in aria-label, (2) default hover shows full integer then muted compact line (Option B), (3) clamp toggle + legend icon + explanation copy, (4) gridline contrast token PR from Arun. Can we track acceptance criteria?
Tyler Nguyen: I'll pick this up. Will create a small RFC and add acceptance criteria + screenshots. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Arun Patel: I'll open the token PR and wire up the aria-labels.
Olivia Ramos: I'll add keyboard focus behavior and accessible copy for screen reader team to review.
Maria Chen: Thanks all - ping me if you need copy tweaks. :thumbsup:
